params.history_window: strictly before the graded week; the graded week is never in the inputs
params.note: margin_sd and total_sd are stated priors, not fitted values: 14 or 15 games per week cannot identify them. They are registered here so a reader can see exactly what produced each probability, and they are not tuned on the graded weeks.

calibration.reading: The model is less accurate than the market on both markets. That does not make a hit rate impossible, but it means any positive result on this capture is not evidence of skill. It is evidence that 15 games is noise.

luck_decomposition.reading: The number to watch is excess_over_model_expectation, not the hit rate. Wins far ABOVE the model's own expectation mean variance flattered it; wins far BELOW mean the model's own probabilities were overconfident and the record was worse than the model predicted. Either way the hit rate alone misleads, in opposite directions.

side.reading: If the share of home picks is far from half, the model is making a directional claim rather than adding noise. Combined with the hit rate, that distinguishes an uninformative model from one whose signal is inverted.

total.reading: If the share of home picks is far from half, the model is making a directional claim rather than adding noise. Combined with the hit rate, that distinguishes an uninformative model from one whose signal is inverted.

side.basis: picked side's own line at open minus the same side's line at close, in points
side.reading: A strategy with a real edge beats the close on most bets. Positive CLV in points means we consistently took the better number. A record that wins while losing at the close is winning on variance.

total.basis: picked side's own line at open minus the same side's line at close, in points
total.reading: A strategy with a real edge beats the close on most bets. Positive CLV in points means we consistently took the better number. A record that wins while losing at the close is winning on variance.

side.staking_basis: flat 1 unit, relayed DraftKings open, push refunded
staking_caveats: Nothing was wagered. This is a paper computation on a relayed price, not obtained profit.
The price is one provider's number at one snapshot. A real fill could be worse, and limits and availability are unknown.
ROI on this sample is dominated by variance: see the sample-size column before reading the number.

leaderboard.name: Side: shrunk rating split, thresholds at half a point
Total: same rating split, thresholds at half a point

gates.name: Price provenance
gates.definition: Every priced row names provider, provider id, source id, https url and retrieval date, and is labelled relayed. PASS if zero rows lack any of these.
gates.evidence: 180 price rows checked, 0 without complete provenance. All rows are relayed via ESPN from provider DraftKings (100); none is operator-direct.

gates.name: Open and close both present
gates.definition: Every originated market carries an opening and a closing observation, so a movement series exists rather than a single stale number.
gates.evidence: 90 market legs, 0 lacking an open or a close.

gates.name: Official result binding
gates.definition: Every priced game binds to an official final score with a source url, and the binding is on the club pair, not on a position in a list.
gates.evidence: 15 of 15 priced games bound to an official final score on the club pair; 0 unbound.

gates.name: Three-column publication
gates.definition: Each board publishes model, market and difference as separate columns, and never omits the market column when the model disagrees.
gates.evidence: 15 side rows each publish model, market and difference separately; 0 rows with a missing column.

gates.name: No synthetic price
gates.definition: No ROI, CLV or edge uses an assumed price such as -110. Where a price is absent the figure is blank and flagged.
gates.evidence: Every ROI and CLV uses a captured price. No -110 or other notional price appears anywhere in the store; where a price is absent the figure is blank.

gates.name: Signal/staking separation
gates.definition: Promotion reads the signal tier only. Staking figures are reported but cannot qualify a strategy. PASS if the promotion function never receives a staking field.
gates.evidence: promote() raises when a staking field is present: staking field(s) ['staking_roi_at_relayed_close'] reached the promotion gate.

gates.name: Sample-size honesty
gates.definition: Every published rate carries n and the n required to detect it at 80% power, so a rate on a small sample is visibly non-evidential.
gates.evidence: 2 strategies each publish n, the n needed at a pre-specified 55% rate (783) and at 60% (194); 0 rows lacking it. n published is 15 and 14, so both are reported as inadequately powered.

gates.name: Push accounting
gates.definition: Pushes are counted and excluded from the hit-rate denominator before the p-value, and the count is published.
gates.evidence: Pushes are counted before the hit rate: 0 on the side board and 0 on the total board. The count is published on the leaderboard.

gates.name: Correlation provenance
gates.definition: Every correlation is computed from official-sourced numbers and publishes its n.
gates.evidence: 4 correlations, each with n and registered source ids; 1 have n at or above 30 and may be ranked. Uneven pairs are shown with their n and marked unrankable.

gates.name: Demotion gate armed
gates.definition: A live strategy carries explicit numeric demotion triggers, evaluated on the live ledger, that send it back to paper. PASS if the rules are numeric and executable.
gates.evidence: Five numeric triggers armed. On a probe ledger all 4 fired, so the gate returns live to paper. No strategy is live yet, so the gate has been exercised but not triggered in production.

demotion_gate.name: Demotion gate (live -> paper)
demotion_gate.holding: demote to paper when any trigger fires
demotion_gate.promotion_back: requires a fresh out-of-sample window that satisfies every promotion gate again

triggers.measures: cumulative flat-stake units from the peak of the live ledger
triggers.why: a live strategy that has given back 20 units at flat stake is not a 2% edge

triggers.measures: hit rate over the most recent 50 settled bets against the promoted rate
triggers.why: a rate that has collapsed over a 50-bet window is stale, not unlucky

triggers.measures: mean closing-line value in basis points over the live ledger
triggers.why: a strategy that consistently loses at the close is on the wrong side of the market, regardless of results

triggers.measures: count of live bets whose captured price failed provenance or reconciliation
triggers.why: one bad price invalidates the ledger it sits in; demote until it is rebuilt

triggers.measures: days since the strategy last cleared every promotion gate on a full re-run
triggers.why: a stale pass is not a pass

paper_to_live.why: below 200 settled bets a 55% rate is inside two standard errors of a coin
the signal, not the stake, decides promotion
the leaderboard tests many strategies; the family-wise error must be controlled
a strategy priced from unverified numbers cannot go live
positive closing-line value is the only forward-looking proof of an edge

correlation_summary.note: Holm-adjusted across the pairs tested in this register. A pair with n below 30 is shown with its n and is not ranked: at n=15 the 95% interval on r spans most of the range, so the point estimate carries almost no information.
